fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). Moses led Israel before Joshua (Joshua 1:1). So this wasn't Joshua winging it like a man with no recipe. He was following the instructions he'd been given.

The elders are there, standing with all Israel in verse 33, but the text never says they asked for the altar. It says Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). Moses led Israel before Joshua (Joshua 1:1). Sometimes the people in the room aren't the people who gave the order.

The Levitical priests do show up in this passage, carrying the ark of the covenant (Joshua 8:33). But the text never says they asked for the altar. It points to Moses, the servant of the LORD, who had commanded it (Joshua 8:31). Good guess, though, because priests and altars do go together.

Uncut is right. The Book of the Law of Moses said, "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). Joshua built it according to what was written. Leaving things exactly as they are is hard for a stamper like me, but Joshua pulled it off.

Carved isn't what the Book said. It called for "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). So the word you want is uncut. I'm a stamper, so I totally get why carving sounds right to me.

Right, the statement is False. Joshua 8:33 says, "All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" Foreigners and citizens alike were in that crowd. Everybody had a spot.

Bless it is! Moses had commanded it earlier, and the text states the purpose plainly: to bless the people of Israel (Joshua 8:33). Half faced Gerizim, half faced Ebal, with the ark between them. That's a whole lot of standing for a good cause.

Kings? That's a fancy guest list, friend! The passage doesn't name any kings among the listeners. It says Joshua read "…before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). So the answer is the women and the little ones.
